commit.message:
Separate equal factor values from a shared generator

Work package 20 of milestone 0.7, the first high finding of the audit of
0.7.0rc5. It stays under 0.7.0rc6, which the profiling commit already
opened.

Candidate inferred from two polynomials being equal that one coordinate
would serve both slots. Those are two different things, and the audit
found both directions of the conflation. The targeted search could not
express a verified step with two distinct coordinates of one value: it
reported its space exhausted after thirty maps although the target was
one step away. And it did build a shared one, which SEA-14 excludes,
naming two coordinates and consuming one without a word. Neither was a
false certificate -- the step holds under BCW-12 -- and both were the
search disagreeing with its own statement of where it looks.

A shared field carries the decision now. enumerate_candidates never sets
it, so equal values there are two coordinates and m = 2;
untargeted_candidates sets it, because UNT-1 wants BCW-12's saving where
an anchor is a square. Both sites say so where they build.

Candidate.factors refuses a surplus of names as well as a shortage. That
is the invariant the audit asked for, and one caller relied on its
absence: scripts/untargeted_space.py handed two names over whatever the
candidate needed, and make measure failed the moment the guard went in.
That is the evidence the silence was worth ending rather than an
argument against the guard, and the script asks for candidate.m now.

Four tests: the m = 2 step being expressible and found, the shared one
staying outside the forward space and reported as a non-answer, the
field defaulting to off and to m = 2 on equal values, and the name
invariant in both directions.

SEA-14 gains the paragraph saying equal values cost two coordinates
here, that sharing is asked for and not inferred, and what each
direction of the conflation did.

commit.message:
Profile the fast suite, and mark one test slow

The fast suite had grown to 139 seconds and the coverage run over it no
longer fitted the assistant's tool budget, so the last two deliveries
argued coverage from a subset instead of running the gate. That is one
step from not running it, which is reason enough to profile rather than
to keep arguing.

One test was a third of the suite. The unweighted control of SEA-14 took
44 seconds, examining 3189 maps since 0.7.0rc5 widened the forward space
by offering both forms of a co-factor. It is now a test of its own rather
than one case of a parametrization over three coefficients, so the two
weighted cases keep their budget of 200 and stay fast, and the control
carries the marker. The suite is 84 seconds and the coverage run over it
208, which fits.

Only one marking, and the profile says of every other candidate why it
stays: the three multi-affine chains are the only check on figures that
stand on three pages, the doctests of docs/api.md are the examples every
public feature is required to have, the hull and the lift of Thompson's
map check published forms, and the hash-seed test is what checks a
determinism claim. Nothing below a second is worth moving, since some
1900 tests share the remaining 30 seconds.

The rule that came out of it is in AGENTS.md beside the timings: a test
earns the marker when the fast suite would otherwise lose more than it
keeps, and a marked test has to be worth running in pytest -m "" rather
than parked there. The control is the only one here on the wrong side of
that, and its docstring says what the marking costs a delivery. It is
the test that says the widening of 0.7.0rc5 added a step without
removing one, so any run touching the targeted enumerator wants it.

commit.message:
Normalize the Jacobian entries, and ask BCW-10 on the support

Work package 19 of milestone 0.7, the second high finding of the audit of
0.7.0rc5, and the version opens 0.7.0rc6. Two causes, one map.

PolyElement.diff leaves a term with a zero coefficient in the sparse
dictionary in positive characteristic: over GF(2) the derivative of
x + x^2 is stored as 0*x + 1, which compares unequal to the ring's one.
Everything downstream compares those entries, so four public operations
broke at once on (x + x^2, y + y^2, z + z^2), a map whose Jacobian is
the identity. carrier_indices was empty; determinant, search and
BCWStep.verify let a raw ExactQuotientFailed out. The entries are
normalized where they are computed, once, and jacobian() was the control
that hid it: sp.Matrix normalizes on the way in, so the matrix was right
while everything reading the entries was not.

carrier_indices_for_factors asked dF_j/dX_j == 1 and claimed that is
BCW-10's "F_j - X_j free of X_j". It is, in characteristic zero. Over
GF(2) that map has the identity for its Jacobian and no displacement
free of its own variable, so the block is the whole map and no
coordinate is a carried factor: the two notions are not the same
question there and neither set contains the other, where I had written
that this one always contains the block. It is decided on the monomial
support now, which is the clause word for word.

The wrong condition came out right by accident, and that is the part
worth naming. The unnormalized derivative compared unequal to one, so
the property returned the empty tuple for a reason that had nothing to
do with the map. Correcting the storage without correcting the condition
would have made it offer three carriers BCW-10 refuses, and the two
findings had to be fixed together or not at all.

I chose the derivative test in work package 16 for consistency with
carrier_indices, when the obligation I was implementing says something
else. Consistency with a neighbour is not a reason to implement a
different condition from the one cited.

tests/test_positive_characteristic.py holds the audit's map against the
Jacobian, both carrier notions, the determinant, a search from the map
to itself and a step that builds and verifies, with a control that
characteristic zero is unchanged. The module says why the two notions
cannot be one predicate, which is the thing the map demonstrates.
